ed6f14df-2849-50ee-95f4-d6b4bb30854e.name: New Schleissheim Palace and Lustheim Palace
ed6f14df-2849-50ee-95f4-d6b4bb30854e.description:
Lustheim Palace, designed in the style of an Italian villa and axially aligned with the Old Palace in a westward direction, has a rectangular ballroom, protruding side-wings with residential rooms, as well as a belvedere above the central wing. The frescos and paintings are all that remain of the originally richly furnished and colourfully decorated interior. According to the concept of a hunting residence, the myth of Diana is illustrated in a number of the ceiling frescos. Her elevation to goddess of the hunt is illustrated on the ceiling of the Banqueting Hall, complemented by other mythological scenes related to her, and surrounded by impressive illusionary architectural features. Today the palace holds a large collection of Meissen porcelain.  
The New Palace was designed to provoke comparison with Versailles and Schönbrunn Palace, incorporating numerous splendid residential rooms and festivity halls, and with its pompous Roman Baroque façade, corresponding to Max Emanuel’s ever-growing claim to power.
ed6f14df-2849-50ee-95f4-d6b4bb30854e.short_description: The impressive summer residence of Elector Max II Emanuel ranks among Bavaria’s major secular Baroque buildings incorporating the Old and New Schleissheim Palace, the hunting seat Lustheim, as well as the palace park and canal system. Competing against Versailles, near Paris, and Schönbrunn Palace, near Vienna, the Elector ordered the construction of a sumptuously decorated palace for which he commissioned famous artists, despite the difficult financial and political situation at that time. Among the highlights are the Great Hall and the Great Gallery. In the latter, according to the patron’s intentions, are displayed masterpieces of European Baroque painting.

ed6f14df-2849-50ee-95f4-d6b4bb30854e.history:
Construction of Lustheim Palace began in 1684 under Bavarian Elector Max II Emanuel probably in anticipation of his marriage to the Emperor’s daughter, Maria Antonia, in 1685. The structure was complete by 1689. During construction of Lustheim Palace, Enrico Zuccalli began drawing the plans for the New Palace, and after redesign, the cornerstone was put in place in 1701.  
Building work stopped briefly in 1704 because of the War of the Spanish Succession. After Max Emanuel’s return from exile in 1715, the new court architect, Joseph Effner, began decoration of the interior in 1719 following French models. Enrico Zuccalli’s design for a novel type of ceremonial staircase was maintained, but then, as the financial situation worsened, plans had to be restrained. The construction was never completed following the death of Bavarian Elector Max II Emanuel in 1726.

fafb3812-1969-5e3a-b9d0-22446066efee.name: Chest for a Portable Altar
fafb3812-1969-5e3a-b9d0-22446066efee.description:
Portable altars in the form of chests were an element of religious furniture, epitomising Portuguese maritime travel to different parts of the world.  
This type of furniture developed from the 16th century onwards as Portuguese maritime voyages, in particular to India and China, increased.  
These voyages often involved both regular and secular clergymen embarking on missionary activities, aristocratic families, the backbone of the administration in the Portuguese empire, or those who set out for diverse corners of the world in the quest for new commercial markets.  
The need to reduce the volume and weight of the cargo transported on these voyages resulted in the construction of furniture that was light and easy to handle and store.  
This piece of furniture is built of wood and covered with black-painted leather. It is adorned with engraved plant motifs and a pattern made out of tacks. On the outside it is fairly plain. The exuberance of the piece is revealed after it is opened and assembled. The internal lining in red silk is further embellished by gold trimming. The fittings that frame the lid were inspired by incised motifs, a decorative mode that flourished during the period.  
The liturgical implements (chalice, crucifix, pyx, cruet, paten and bell), all of which were necessary to celebrate mass, were stored in a drawer below the altar table, in customised, made-to-measure indentations.  
Many masses were celebrated aboard the carracks on altars such as this one, as well as on land, at sites that did not have suitable facilities for religious worship.  
Mass could only be celebrated on altars that contained an altar-stone – a stone that had been blessed – upon which was placed the chalice and the host. In this altar, the altar-stone is found in a concave indentation within the table.  
During voyages, priests were obliged to celebrate mass every Sunday and on holy days. A particular feature of masses celebrated on board ship was that they did not have the consecration and consequently did not have communion. They were thus called “dry masses”.  
In his work, *As* *Cartas Ânuas da China: 1636, 1643 a 1649,* a compilation of letters from China written to the Jesuit General in Rome annually, the Jesuit priest António de Gouveia described the presence of altars in the houses of Portuguese settlers. He relates that it was a common practice to “assemble the altar” in the largest room so that mass could be held.

fc45efc5-13ac-52a6-acca-d9f0c752a728.name: Episcopal residence, Kroměříž
fc45efc5-13ac-52a6-acca-d9f0c752a728.alternate_name: Kremsier, known as the Athens of the Haná region
fc45efc5-13ac-52a6-acca-d9f0c752a728.description: This residential complex for the bishops of Olomouc consists of a chateau with a lower garden and a floral garden. Canonical homes line the street leading to the Church of St. Mauritz, which contains a chapel in which bishops were interred. The chateau, with a closed central courtyard, is a free-standing building with four wings and two floors on a trapezoid ground plan.
fc45efc5-13ac-52a6-acca-d9f0c752a728.short_description: Originally a market village, Kroměříž grew up around the crossroads of major European trade routes. Moravian bishops purchased the demesne in 1107. The residential complex consists of a chateau with a lower garden, floral garden and canonical homes lining the street leading to the Church of St. Mauritz. A fresco by F. A. Maulbertsch in the Feudal Hall is considered the most impressive of its kind in Central Europe. In 1998 the Kroměříž gardens and chateau were included on the UNESCO World Heritage List.
fc45efc5-13ac-52a6-acca-d9f0c752a728.method_for_datation: A number of receipts, contracts and correspondence associated with the monument have survived. Additional information for the dating of individual stages is provided by historical events and biographies of the bishops.

fc45efc5-13ac-52a6-acca-d9f0c752a728.history: Originally a market village, Kroměříž grew up around the crossroads of the Amber and Salt Trails, two major European trade routes. Moravian bishops purchased the demesne in 1107. Bruno of Schaumburk (d.1281) built a Gothic castle and established the Chapter of St. Mauritz. In 1290 Kroměříž was granted town status. Under Stanislav Thurzo (d.1540), a man of humanist leanings, the castle was converted into a Renaissance chateau and a summer residence. In 1643 the town was plundered by the Swedes and burnt down during the Wallachian uprising of 1821. The famous picture gallery, now containing work by L. Cranach and one of Titian’s last paintings, was built around the end of the 17th century.

040b2846-3c5d-576f-85cf-a8f925d606cd.name: Virgin Mary with Child Handing the Order Gown to St. Norbert in the Presence of St. Augustine
040b2846-3c5d-576f-85cf-a8f925d606cd.description: This side altar altarpiece is typical of Leicher, Maulbertsch’s associate and frequent collaborator. The layout, colour scheme and movements of the figures in an S-shaped composition, reflect Maulbertsch’s expressive style although transposed to a softer, more lyrical outcome. The presence of St. Norbert, founder of the Premonstratensian order, refers to the “mother” monastery in Louka. The subject of the picture is the vision of St. Norbert in Prémontré when he saw the Virgin Mary, who gave her blessing to his intention to establish a monastery there, and handed him a white monastic gown.
040b2846-3c5d-576f-85cf-a8f925d606cd.location: Pilgrimage Church of the Scourged Saviour, Dyje, side altar

073a3608-7fb8-5a06-99a1-807b858158d2.name: Chapel of Mercy, interior
073a3608-7fb8-5a06-99a1-807b858158d2.description: At the start of the comprehensive Baroque refurbishment work the master builder Gallus Gratl from Inzig erected a Chapel of Mercy on an oval ground plan at the site where, according to legend, herdsman worshipped the miracle-working image of the Virgin Mary, a small clothed statue of the Mother of God from the period around 1400. Piers with pilaster projections support a domical vault, interspersed with open semi-circular arches; in the cupola there is an oval opening. The Chapel of Mercy is thus to be understood as a homage to the Roman Pantheon which has been a Church of Mary since the 6th century.
073a3608-7fb8-5a06-99a1-807b858158d2.location: West nave, axial in the centre

0c30fb7d-3f55-524f-acdd-1883685cccae.name: Stucco ceiling
0c30fb7d-3f55-524f-acdd-1883685cccae.description: The stucco ceiling, presumably also from Gigl, displays slightly different motifs and ornamentation compared to the façades. The border area is composed of intricately intertwined bands with acanthus leaves; in the centre, framed by strap and vine scroll decoration, is a star composed of bands, leaves and shells. Above the entrance to the bay window the coat of arms of the Fischer family.
0c30fb7d-3f55-524f-acdd-1883685cccae.location: Corner room on the third floor (living quarters)

0d0e56db-22c0-5b6c-94fa-3c424bf11d56.name: The Choir or Sala do Tesouro
0d0e56db-22c0-5b6c-94fa-3c424bf11d56.description: Probably used by the nuns as a meeting place, the floor is of inlaid Brazilian wood. The chapel contains several reliquaries within gilded wooden frames above the choir stalls. Above one of the doors there is a tabernacle with the coat of arms of King José I. The Window bays are adorned with *azulejos*, while the ceiling and walls are decorated with paintings of the Life of Christ and the Life of the Virgin Mary of the 17th and 18th centuries.
0d0e56db-22c0-5b6c-94fa-3c424bf11d56.artist: Marcos da Cruz [n.d.], Bento Coelho da Silveira (1648–1708), André Gonçalves (1685–1762)

0e176e66-89ab-5988-b754-f76492d554b6.name: Rondel
0e176e66-89ab-5988-b754-f76492d554b6.description:
The concept of a garden outside the town walls was probably proposed by F. Luchese. It was executed under the guidance of G. P. Tencalla, with M. A. Lublinský participating in the design. The original state of the gardens is captured in a portfolio by J. van den Nypoort. The ground-plan of the ornamental garden contained a complex water system, feeding ponds, fountains, an aviary, a lake, and a series of “water jets” with which the bishop had become acquainted in Salzburg. The axis of the ornamental garden runs from the skittle-alley entrance that opens onto two “strawberry mounds”. The mounds originate in ancient gardens where they were artificially heaped (Khorsabad) with gazebos, as was the case in Kromeríž. At one time the axis of the garden was flanked by labyrinths and rectangular ponds.  
Rising out of the intersection of paths in the geometrically segmented garden there is a rotunda covered with stucco in high relief. The central space is divided into four grottos and four salons that once featured fountains. Statues and paintings depicting satyrs, allegories of the seasons and stories from Ovid's *Metamorphoses* line the gallery that closes off the front of the garden. The sculptures are modelled on the Villa Pamphilli in Rome. Alternating male and female figures in niches represent ancient gods and goddesses, muses and historical figures from ancient Rome. Side walls once contained grottos with water cascades. A Latin inscription over the main entrance invites visitors to view what was once wetland and wasteland but which now, after many years of hard labour and considerable cost, is a garden designed to delight present and future generations.
0e176e66-89ab-5988-b754-f76492d554b6.artist: Giovanni Pietro Tencalla (1629 Bissone? – 1702 Vienna?), Quirico Castelli (Lugano? active 1658–1672), Carpoforo Tencalla (1623–1685, Bissone), Michael Mandík (? Gdaňsk, worked 1689–1699 in Moravia)

0e7a534f-4091-5533-9e34-fa83788eea0c.name: Chapel of the Sorrowful Mother (Fieger Chapel)
0e7a534f-4091-5533-9e34-fa83788eea0c.description: Built as an extension to the vestibule, it was donated Johann Karl Graf Fieger. Together with the magnificent column altar, the most significant feature is the ceiling frescos from Kaspar Waldmann, a glorification of Mary with the seven founders of the Servite Order and scenes from the life of Mary.
0e7a534f-4091-5533-9e34-fa83788eea0c.location: Northern vestibule, The Servite Monastery Church of St. Charles Borromeo

0f4907e8-1bfe-5be4-9774-f6308f10d7a4.name: Pulpit
0f4907e8-1bfe-5be4-9774-f6308f10d7a4.description: Dark-bated oak pulpit with busts depicting Jesus Christ, the Virgin Mary and Saints Cajetan and Andreas Avellinus.

130a251d-cd8c-55de-81ca-2e58a7733c0b.name: St. Gregory
130a251d-cd8c-55de-81ca-2e58a7733c0b.description: Illusionary architecture and ornamentation make up a major part of the church decoration. They also provide a background for one of the Church Fathers in a vault joint. St. Gregory is a crypto-portrait of his namesake, Řehoř Lambeck, a benefactor of the church and art-loving abbot of Louka Monastery. J. Winterhalder Jr., a pupil and close associate of Maulbertsch, participated in the painting of the Church Fathers, Prophets and Evangelists.
130a251d-cd8c-55de-81ca-2e58a7733c0b.location: Pilgrimage Church of the Scourged Saviour, Dyje, detail of the Fresco
130a251d-cd8c-55de-81ca-2e58a7733c0b.artist: Franz Anton Maulbertsch (1724 Langenargen am Bodensee – 1796 Vienna) – Josef Winterhalder Jr. (1743 Vöhrenbach – 1807 Znojmo)

14cf3ac9-f201-5ffe-96c6-9da83f2f8352.name: Library Façade
14cf3ac9-f201-5ffe-96c6-9da83f2f8352.description: Magnificent Baroque façade in limestone with four huge columns crowned by the royal coat of arms and the phrase “So highly are books praised here in Coimbra that a library crowns the city head”.

169326c2-920f-568e-865b-5feb37a401c0.name: Count’s Study
169326c2-920f-568e-865b-5feb37a401c0.description: The “Chinese” room was adjoined by a library. The floor, inlaid with several kinds of wood, was by the court joiner. The count consulted with the Viennese adviser, Conrad Adolph von Albrecht, who also worked for the Sinzendorfs in Židlochovice in most of his artistic activities.
169326c2-920f-568e-865b-5feb37a401c0.artist: Jacob Prandtauer (1660 Stanz – 1726 St. Pölten), Johann Friedrich Praetorius

16b7443b-221e-5c2f-b518-f5af41d929f0.name: Large Dining Hall (Assembly Hall)
16b7443b-221e-5c2f-b518-f5af41d929f0.description: Due to the death of Bishop Egkh, the Large Dining Hall spanning two floors was not renovated. Some of Maulbertsch's preparatory sketches, with scenes from Ovid's *Metamorphoses* featuring allegories of the times of the day, have, however, survived. The hall was further enhanced in the spirit of Rococo Classicism under Bishop Hamilton, although not with murals but with gilded stuccos portraying allegories of the sciences and arts, together with the canvases *The Trial of Paris* and *The Wedding of Peleus and Thetis*, exemplifying ephemeral vanity, and *Pallas Athena Kidnapping an Ephebus from Aphrodite*, symbolising wisdom and stability. The alternative name of the room, the Assembly Hall, comes from 1848 when an imperial assembly took place there.
16b7443b-221e-5c2f-b518-f5af41d929f0.artist: Franz Adolph of Freenthal (1721–1773), Karl Martin Keller

1806be4b-9dfd-5bdf-9314-0f98c01bc8cd.name: Chapel of St. Anastasia
1806be4b-9dfd-5bdf-9314-0f98c01bc8cd.description: Marble columns connected elegantly by arches support a vault decorated with virtuous Rocaille stucco, on which is painted the vision of St. Anastasia’s ascension into heaven. The high-quality Venetian altarpiece of the main altar illustrates the intercession of saints to pilgrims with illnesses of the head and mental diseases of all kinds. Capriccio-like  side altars by the hand of the famous sculptor  Ignaz Günther complete the precious decoration.
1806be4b-9dfd-5bdf-9314-0f98c01bc8cd.location: At the north side of the abbey church nearby the chancel and sacristy
1806be4b-9dfd-5bdf-9314-0f98c01bc8cd.artist: Architecture: Johann Michael Fischer(1692–1766); stucco and high altar: Johann Michael Feichtmayr (1696–1772); side altars: Ignaz Günther (1725–75); altarpieces for the altars of St. Anastasia and of the Immaculate Conception: Jacopo Amigoni (1682–1752); ceiling fresco: Johann Jakob Zeiller (1710–83)

1a5ad99e-4e60-596e-9113-8c0b78eebfe2.name: Large reading tables
1a5ad99e-4e60-596e-9113-8c0b78eebfe2.description: The six large tables (buffets) in multi-coloured and exotic woods are all slightly different and designed to match each room.
1a5ad99e-4e60-596e-9113-8c0b78eebfe2.location: Interior, Biblioteca Joanina da Universidade de Coimbra

1b76ee67-59f5-5426-ae90-e4aff6200791.name: Electress’s Private Chapel
1b76ee67-59f5-5426-ae90-e4aff6200791.description: Panelled with scagliola marble, the chapel flaunts its sumptuous ornamental decoration. To great effect, the ceiling, decorated with interlacing stuccowork, opens into an oval lantern displaying a fresco of heaven. The valuable altarpiece comes from the workshop of Peter Paul Rubens.
1b76ee67-59f5-5426-ae90-e4aff6200791.location: New Palace, first floor of the north wing

1d2c211d-2700-5a80-817e-a40c9d14229c.name: Oratories
1d2c211d-2700-5a80-817e-a40c9d14229c.description: Oratory of Our Lady of the Rosary constructed from wood and canvas. There are others dedicated to Our Lady of Mount Carmel, St. Matthew, and St. John the Baptist. With the exception of the Oratory of St. John the Baptist, the outside wings are adorned with paintings.

2dd05ca7-8405-5c54-83a9-e8196103e37b.name: Altar of St. Benedict (high altar of the abbey church)
2dd05ca7-8405-5c54-83a9-e8196103e37b.description: The high altar, including the interior façade of the sacristy and the monk’s choir through the figure niches, is the oldest part of the valuable furnishing of the abbey church with marble altars. In the course of time, the columned aedicule of the retable was supplemented by a tabernacle and a new altarpiece that shows St. Benedict, the founder of the order, together with his sister Scholastica, as well as by an attic, the large clock of which is a reminder of the passing of time.
2dd05ca7-8405-5c54-83a9-e8196103e37b.dates:
1686 mensa, retable, and sculptures in niches  
1696 tabernacle  
1788 altarpiece  
1790 attic of the retable and tabernacle figures
2dd05ca7-8405-5c54-83a9-e8196103e37b.artist: Architecture of the altar: Johann Georg Guggemos (1636–1703); sculptures in niches and angels: Balthasar Ableithner (1614–1705); architecture of the tabernacle: Abbot Eliland Öttl (gov. 1690–1707); tabernacle figures: Roman Anton Boos (1733–1810); attic of the retable: Franz Edmund Doll (1744–1824); altarpiece: Martin Knoller (1725–1804)

2eb1f102-370e-5a15-aa76-966aead4921b.name: Ceiling fresco of the Great Hall
2eb1f102-370e-5a15-aa76-966aead4921b.description: The ceiling fresco of the Great Hall was once the world’s largest. Illustrating the fight between Aeneas and Turnus for the hand of the king’s daughter Lavinia, Aeneas, it is sometimes said resembles the Elector Max II Emanuel. The use of a painted landscape background instead of *trompe-l’oeil* architectural decoration was novel at the time.
2eb1f102-370e-5a15-aa76-966aead4921b.location: New Palace, first floor of the central wing

32a8ad1d-7f6d-50f5-86ce-2904db9b8e81.name: Façade
32a8ad1d-7f6d-50f5-86ce-2904db9b8e81.description: The façade, whose towers, gables and escutcheons were first completed in 1900, i.e. supplemented, most clearly show the influence of the Salzburg Dome. The exterior is maintained in the strict arrangement typical of South German Early Baroque. The towers and the centre of the façade form a unit. The two portal arches, separated by double pilasters (cf. St. Michael’s Church, Munich) already anticipate the configuration of the interior nave walls.

32b1e458-9669-5b2a-91d1-0cb33372a953.name: The lateral altars of the Chapterhouse
32b1e458-9669-5b2a-91d1-0cb33372a953.description: These were perhaps, originally, part of the main chapel and sacristy until the reign of King João III (1521–1557). The two lateral altars were installed during the reigns of King João V (r.1706–1750) and King José I (r.1750–1777). One is dedicated to the Death of Christ the other to Our Lady of Good Death.
32b1e458-9669-5b2a-91d1-0cb33372a953.location: Connected to the nave of the church

37d69274-1d0d-51a0-8b8a-bd4be92b778e.name: Paintings and *azulejos* of the nave and main chapel
37d69274-1d0d-51a0-8b8a-bd4be92b778e.description:
The 20 ceiling paintings depicting the Life of the Virgin are by the Marcos da Cruz workshop. The walls are adorned with paintings by Bento Coelho da Silveira. They depict the Life of St. Claire (upper register) and the Life of St. Francis (lower register). Paintings by André Gonçalves decorate the triumphal arch. These feature the Coronation of the Virgin by the Holy Trinity. Paintings of St. Claire and St. Francis flank the archway. The nave *azulejos* are by the Dutch artist, Willem van der Kloet; they were commissioned in Holland. Close to the *rocaille* pulpit are *azulejos* featuring Franciscan monks praying. The *azulejos* in the main chapel are by Jan van Oort.  
These depict the vision of Pope Nicholas V when standing by the body of St. Francis.
37d69274-1d0d-51a0-8b8a-bd4be92b778e.dates: Ceiling paintings: c.1675–1690; triumphal arch paintings: c.1740–50; *azulejos*: 1698–1707; pulpit: 1747–1759; main altar: after 1755
37d69274-1d0d-51a0-8b8a-bd4be92b778e.location: Nave and main chapel, Church and Convent of Madre de Deus
37d69274-1d0d-51a0-8b8a-bd4be92b778e.artist: Painters: Marcos da Cruz [n.d.], Bento Coelho da Silveira (1648–1708), André Gonçalves (1685–1762); tile painters: Jan van Oort [n.d.], Willem van der Kloet [n.d.], Gabriel del Barco (1649–c.1703); woodcarver: Félix Adauto da Cunha (1649–c.1703)

414c7c6c-2207-59d9-bb8a-cc731e96b803.name: Entrance frontage
414c7c6c-2207-59d9-bb8a-cc731e96b803.description: Construction of the college started in around 1593 and continued throughout the 17th century. The church tower was left unfinished for some time and so that on entering the church the visitor may note its two major building phases and changes of style spanning some 150 years.
414c7c6c-2207-59d9-bb8a-cc731e96b803.location: Jesuit Church of the Assumption of the Virgin Mary
414c7c6c-2207-59d9-bb8a-cc731e96b803.artist: Antonio Gabri, Mořic Grimm (1669 Achtdorf – 1757 Brno)

4245f4f1-ced8-58b2-8737-09920f72fa22.name: Interior
4245f4f1-ced8-58b2-8737-09920f72fa22.description: General view of the interior of the church. There is a huge representation of Calvary with life-size figures at the main altar.
4245f4f1-ced8-58b2-8737-09920f72fa22.location: Bom Jesus Church, Bom Jesus de Braga Sanctuary (Bom Jesus do Monte)

46629869-175a-5ce1-8e92-45a1b32d5f70.name: Hall of the Ancestors
46629869-175a-5ce1-8e92-45a1b32d5f70.description: The wainscoting, a copy of the imperial office in Vienna, features family portraits by leading Viennese portraitists including J. Kupecký. The vaulting is decorated with the painting *The Celebration of Jaroměřice*, framed by illusionary architecture.
46629869-175a-5ce1-8e92-45a1b32d5f70.artist: Josef Emanuel Fischer von Erlach (1656–1742 Vienna?), Tobias Gravani, Johann Gotfried Auerbach, Johann Baptist Glunck, Martin Meytens (1695 Stockholm – 1770 Vienna), Domenico Maria Francia, Alessandro Ferretti

4692d873-94e6-59eb-9dc0-1830c1081690.name: Ceiling fresco
4692d873-94e6-59eb-9dc0-1830c1081690.description: Guglielmi’s high-grade ceiling fresco depicts allegories of the Four Continents but doesn’t leave any doubt about the supremacy of Europe. Again, the topic shows a clear connection to the life and work of the patron. In the centre of the painting stands Mercury, the god of trade, with a cornucopia. The theme is trade and its worldwide power spreading European comforts, announced by Fame, all over the world. The accentuated exotic design of the figures corresponds with the painted over-doors in the ballroom.

4721206d-edec-5f4f-8475-830cfd0d5bb0.name: Crucifix
4721206d-edec-5f4f-8475-830cfd0d5bb0.description: The cross, created by the sculptor of Stams Monastery, Andreas Thamasch in the year of his death, is a “wound” or “Blutheilands” crucifix and is also referred to as a “Plague Cross”. With his last work Thamasch succeeded in creating an especially expressive example of this type; the stirring face wracked with torment, the body covered with wounds.

47be1ddd-0ecd-5944-937b-603bf7067790.name: The Virgin Mary as Queen of Heaven
47be1ddd-0ecd-5944-937b-603bf7067790.description: In 1736–1745 the church was redecorated. The vaults are covered with fresco paintings. The Coronation of the Virgin Mary (Queen of Heaven) is in the chancel while in the naves are the Celebrations of Christ, the Holy Spirit and the Virgin Mary along with other works. The artist was a pupil of C. D. Assam, a leading south-German fresco painter who was active in Munich in around 1720. He came to Silesia and Moravia through the Order of German Knights and in 1743 he became court painter to Count Filip Ludvík of Sinzendorf.
47be1ddd-0ecd-5944-937b-603bf7067790.location: Jesuit Church of the Assumption of the Virgin Mary

48d6ab89-fd69-5029-ab77-89ea887fd268.name: Façade
48d6ab89-fd69-5029-ab77-89ea887fd268.description: The side façade with its five axes and window axes at irregular intervals only has one central polygonal bay window. Horizontally it is concluded by an eaves cornice. The stucco, forming an embellishment around the window openings, has more room to unfold than on the main façade. The architectural forms of the décor, such as the window moulding, are overshadowed by the vigorous outgrowth of ornamentation.

49f2b9ac-02d2-5d5a-b795-331d46920de1.name: Altar of St. Cajetan
49f2b9ac-02d2-5d5a-b795-331d46920de1.description: The altar bears a masterpiece of German Baroque painting dedicated to the founder of the Theatine order.

514d8dc0-868f-5204-a073-0bc44b2dabbb.name: Robillion Pavilion
514d8dc0-868f-5204-a073-0bc44b2dabbb.description: Designed by Robillion, the Pavilion is sometimes considered one of Portugal's first Neo-Classical buildings. However, it is no more than an expression of the *French* Baroque – obviously more “Classical” – attached to the overall palace form. It has two floors and a considerable monumentality, emphasised by the Stairway of the Lions.

53f0ae70-9e34-55bc-bbcb-4ee9c86e09a0.name: Stucco
53f0ae70-9e34-55bc-bbcb-4ee9c86e09a0.description: The stuccowork, executed during 1634–7, is the work of Georg Braun of the Wessobrun school according to designs from Hans Schor and Florian Nut. Panels, vases, festoons, and draperies, framed by rod motifs, underscore the structural elements in emulation of the austere panelled stucco of the South German (Munich) style. The transept and choir also contain ornaments in the emerging scrollwork style, designed c. 1640/50 by Oswald Kaiser.
53f0ae70-9e34-55bc-bbcb-4ee9c86e09a0.artist: Georg Braun [n.d.], Hans Schor (1585–1674), Florian Nut [n.d.], Frair Oswald Kaiser [n.d.]

5bc76a0c-5131-5c24-99d0-666fd90caf59.name: Allegory of Salvation
5bc76a0c-5131-5c24-99d0-666fd90caf59.description: The middle section of the vault is the centre of the longitudinal building and the principal part of its iconography. Adam and Eve embody the burden of eternal sin and mortality. Archangel Gabriel wreathed in flower garlands bears the Divine message of the salvation of mankind – the birth of Christ and his sacrifice – symbolised by a cross and the marks of Christ’s torture. The scene of the Supreme Divine Secret – where the Word becomes the body – closes with Archangel Michael weighing souls on Judgement Day. The arrival of the Saviour as foretold by the prophets is represented in the joints of the vault with Moses, Abraham, Noah and Enoch.
5bc76a0c-5131-5c24-99d0-666fd90caf59.location: Pilgrimage Church of the Scourged Saviour, Dyje, detail of the Fresco
5bc76a0c-5131-5c24-99d0-666fd90caf59.artist: Franz Anton Maulbertsch (1724 Langenargen am Bodensee – 1796 Vienna)

5c1e94cf-ce7a-5555-9256-3d473268fb97.name: Portal
5c1e94cf-ce7a-5555-9256-3d473268fb97.description: The college complex was pulled down in 1904 during the redevelopment of Brno. Only a photographic record and a portal from the Cardinal’s Courtyard, found today next to the church presbytery, has survived. The statue of Archangel Michael on the ledge holds cartouches with the coat of arms of Cardinal František of Dietrichstein. On the sides are statues of Saints, Ignatius of Loyola, founder of the Jesuit order, and Francis Xaverius. A plaque installed later commemorates the academy of 1778.
5c1e94cf-ce7a-5555-9256-3d473268fb97.location: Jesuit Church of the Assumption of the Virgin Mary
5c1e94cf-ce7a-5555-9256-3d473268fb97.artist: Jan Křtitel Erna (1625?, Brno – 1698, Brno) – Jan Kašpar Pröbstl (? – 1729, Brno)

5c94a693-94d2-5ebe-82b9-608c53f0f3fd.name: High altar
5c94a693-94d2-5ebe-82b9-608c53f0f3fd.description: The imposing high altar with six columns above a concave ground plan was altered considerably in the late 19th century and subsequently returned to its original form during restoration work concluded in 1982. The original altarpiece, the *Assumption of Mary* painted by Franz Laukas in 1724, was also reinserted. The two masterfully executed statues of St. Joseph and Joachim, the work of Andreas Köll (c. 1720) were also repainted white.

65e0961f-c135-53b7-936d-31d97f565267.name: Ceiling fresco: *The Veneration of St. Charles Borromeo*
65e0961f-c135-53b7-936d-31d97f565267.description: The frescos in Volders are among the most important of Knoller’s works. The apotheosis of the church patron in the main cupola is the high point of the programme, surrounded by scenes from his life. As an important representative of the Counter Reformation his veneration goes hand in hand with the victory of Catholicism. Knoller’s clear composition with monumental figures already contains elements of Classicism.
65e0961f-c135-53b7-936d-31d97f565267.location: Main cupola, The Servite Monastery Church of St. Charles Borromeo

6a906d8b-0bc1-5f1f-959d-21eda46497c4.name: Gilded carvings
6a906d8b-0bc1-5f1f-959d-21eda46497c4.description: Vine leaves, bunches of grapes, plumage-shaped acanthus leaves and *phoenixes*, combined with seraphs and musician angels, frame not only the exuberant oval frame of the High and Low Choir but also the six oil on canvas paintings and the two large windows placed each side of the nave.

6be75fcb-c136-5464-b836-1965beae6a26.name: Façade
6be75fcb-c136-5464-b836-1965beae6a26.description: The entire idiosyncrasy and fancy of the Early Baroque building can be best seen on the façade which appears as if it was pieced together from a construction kit composed of the most bizarre forms. The departure from the classical theory of form shows that the dilettante architect (= enthusiast) was still an adherent of Mannerism, drawing his vocabulary of forms from religious tracts. Little of the often classical austerity of German Early Baroque is in evidence here. The chapels at the sides of the façade were added later in accordance with the existing design.

6f0f07b0-eee8-503e-a5b8-02651b202a00.name: General view of the Stairway of the Five Senses and the Fountain of Vision  and of  Taste
6f0f07b0-eee8-503e-a5b8-02651b202a00.description: This stairway continues the theme of the hierarchy of the five senses, as if revealing in the ascending course the degree of corporeity that should be attributed to each of the senses. The mythological figures found at the axis of the fountain were re-“Christianised” by order of the Censorial Court in 1774 having previously been considered “indecorous” due to their proximity to the biblical figures. The figures – whose original denominations are well known – were maintained and only the inscriptions were changed.
6f0f07b0-eee8-503e-a5b8-02651b202a00.location: The Stairway of the Five Senses, Bom Jesus de Braga Sanctuary (Bom Jesus do Monte)

6f69a47e-294c-59c1-8a2b-a6157999fccc.name: Pulpit
6f69a47e-294c-59c1-8a2b-a6157999fccc.description: The richly decorated pulpit in the scrollwork style, donated by Claudia de’ Medici c. 1640 (monogram “C” with crown), is attributed to the Jesuit Friar Oswald Kaiser.

718b140c-3c37-56e7-9342-578e4be4a043.name: Main façade
718b140c-3c37-56e7-9342-578e4be4a043.description: Four storeys, each with three window axes, extend above two compact Late Gothic access arches, with the central axis symmetrically framed by two polygonal bay windows. The building is crowned by a Baroque valley roof gable with volutes and a vertical oval window in the centre. The bold stucco composed of garlands of flowers and fruit, festoons, shells and putti, linked by foliage and strapwork, establish an unusually sculptural accent, thus giving expression to the wealth and prestige of the building’s owner.

74c6cc96-1064-598d-8fdd-a09d0c9171cf.name: Chapel of St. John the Baptist
74c6cc96-1064-598d-8fdd-a09d0c9171cf.description: The Chapel of St. John the Baptist, with its lavishly ornamented surfaces in coloured marble and other stone facings, is in the Roman Baroque style. The bronze gates of the front balustrade and the bronze side doors display the monogram of King João V. The side panels – the Annunciation (right) and Pentecost (left) – and the central panel – The Baptism of Christ – as well as the floor (displaying an armillary sphere), are mosaics. Several types of ornamental stone are used in the chapel. An important collection of liturgical objects was produced as part of the interior decoration project: gold-embroidered vestments, several metal objects – candleholders, reliquaries and crucifixes – and also books for the Mass.
74c6cc96-1064-598d-8fdd-a09d0c9171cf.dates: The interior decoration of the chapel was commissioned from Rome in 1740 by King João V (1706–50) and constructed between 1742 and 1750, when it was officially inaugurated in Lisbon.
74c6cc96-1064-598d-8fdd-a09d0c9171cf.location: Church Interior, Church of São Roque
74c6cc96-1064-598d-8fdd-a09d0c9171cf.artist: In Rome architects Luigi Vanvitelli (1700–1773) and Niccolò Salvi (1697–1751) directed hundreds of artists and craftsmen; Mosaic: Agostino Masucci (1691–1758) and Mattia Moretti (d. 1779); Floor mosaic: Enrico Enuo.

7bb2bdb2-91ed-584a-9b73-434103abc508.name: *Sala terrena*
7bb2bdb2-91ed-584a-9b73-434103abc508.description: Of the 17th-century interiors, only a hall opening to the garden and flanked by two grottos has survived the many fires. Stuccos frame allegorical pictures of Earth and Heaven, the Four Seasons and the Elements, symbolised by mythological figures. The decoration is the work of M. A. Lublinský, artist, canon, and advisor to the bishop.
7bb2bdb2-91ed-584a-9b73-434103abc508.artist: Baldassare Fontana (1661–1733, Chiasso), Paolo Pagani (1655 Castello Valsolda – 1716 Milan)

7d79aec6-af13-5110-a27e-45a7ec8a4d19.name: Fountain of the Five Holy Wounds
7d79aec6-af13-5110-a27e-45a7ec8a4d19.description: The motto for the theme of the senses is given by the first fountain, which refers precisely to the Suffering of Christ, and presents the symbolism that summarises the *Via Crucis*: The Five Holy Wounds Fountain. The fountain tablet presents in relief the instruments of the Passion of Christ.
7d79aec6-af13-5110-a27e-45a7ec8a4d19.location: The Stairway of the Five Senses, Bom Jesus de Braga Sanctuary (Bom Jesus do Monte)

81361e9e-cd2c-5f12-afd9-bc76a3a86457.name: The Annunciation
81361e9e-cd2c-5f12-afd9-bc76a3a86457.description: The niches in the side naves contain a series of eight pictures with scenes from the Life of the Virgin Mary. This was commissioned for the newly built Jesuit church and Marian congregation by the Count of Dietrichstein. The Marian congregation was originally to consist of Italian craftsmen and merchants. Domestic artistic output was unable to comply with the demands of the donors and the new functions of the commissions, however, so the gap was filled by Italian stonemasons and sculptors arriving in Moravia from the late 16th century onwards, and artists of Flemish origin whose style was informed by P. P. Rubens, and who met the requirements of Re-Catholicization. The monumental *Madonna* (1670) in the Chapel of the Virgin Mary is by Jan van der Furth, a Flemish sculptor, active in Brno.
81361e9e-cd2c-5f12-afd9-bc76a3a86457.location: Jesuit Church of the Assumption of the Virgin Mary
81361e9e-cd2c-5f12-afd9-bc76a3a86457.artist: Baldissere di Anna (1560, Venezia – after 1639, Venezia)

8817f196-3685-51fa-b249-38607df00ba9.name: Northern side façade
8817f196-3685-51fa-b249-38607df00ba9.description: Religious motifs are no longer to be found on the side façades instead they are completely devoted to the amusement of the viewer. While the south side features a false window with a woman looking out, the north side is largely decorated with exotic animals in accordance with the fashion of the time. Three monkeys are sitting on the cornice with a basket of fruit, above them a parrot on a stick and a cat at the other end of the cornice.

89c05fc9-f779-5631-bd7e-77ed9cf6185a.name: Altarpiece: *Baptism of the Indian Nobleman* and *St. Francis Xavier’s Miracle of the Crab*
89c05fc9-f779-5631-bd7e-77ed9cf6185a.description: The altarpieces of the side chapel dedicated to St. Francis Xavier, glorify him as the most important missionary of the Jesuit order, who, like Ignatius, was conferred sainthood in 1622. The painting depicting the baptism of the Indian nobleman is attributed to Johann Heinrich Schönfeld, together with the scene on the rear wall of the miracle of the crab in which Francis Xavier received his crucifix back from the sea. The images refer to the Jesuit order as the main bearer of the missionary counter-reformation.
89c05fc9-f779-5631-bd7e-77ed9cf6185a.location: First right-hand side chapel, Jesuit Church Innsbruck

8b8d95b0-01c3-5050-9691-e08552b65528.name: Scourged Christ
8b8d95b0-01c3-5050-9691-e08552b65528.description: The miraculous statue was brought by a monk to Louka Monastery from the Steingaden Monastery in Bavaria. It is a replica of an Adoration statue in the local *Wieskirche*. The statue was first placed on a side altar in the old Church of St. Lawrence where it was believed to heal the sick and enjoyed enormous respect. When a new church was built on the site the statue was installed at the high altar. The church decoration was determined by the new dedication to the Scourged Christ.
8b8d95b0-01c3-5050-9691-e08552b65528.location: Pilgrimage Church of the Scourged Saviour, Dyje

8b96a363-f446-5109-9d02-c46824b4fd8c.name: Entrance portal
8b96a363-f446-5109-9d02-c46824b4fd8c.description: The chateau was renovated under K. Liechtenstein-Castelkorn, at first to a design by F. Luchese, but after his death, to the designs of G. P. Tencalla. The current state of the facades (largely respecting Tencalla’s approach) is the result of a restoration, following a fire in 1752, by Cyrani of Bolleshaus and later F. A. Krzoupal. The courtyard was approached in the same manner as the external facades while the courtyard arcade has been walled-up. The facade features tall pilasters alternating with continuous window axes.

92a08715-2350-530f-b788-77727a9408e0.name: Sculptures of the chancel screen
92a08715-2350-530f-b788-77727a9408e0.description: Towards the end of World War II the entire choir area was destroyed by fire, including the high altar, the choir screen and the tabernacle. Of the four evangelist figures flanking the passageways through to the choir, only Marcus, John and Lucas have remained intact. They are counted among the most accomplished Baroque sculptures in Bavaria.

95109161-87b5-5953-88a1-413967eb4236.name: Ceiling Painting
95109161-87b5-5953-88a1-413967eb4236.description: The original ceiling painting comprising architectural elements was made by the Spanish painter Francisco Venegas at the end of the 16th century. The Triumph of the Holy Cross, among other scenes from the bible, were mostly inspired by engravings from Antwerp and added in the early 17th century by the Portuguese painter, Amaro do Vale.

9767c365-8093-52c3-83c1-3946d0072faa.name: View from the east
9767c365-8093-52c3-83c1-3946d0072faa.description: Although the arrangement of the rest of the building is not as closely crowded as the façade, the walls are still un-classical in their configuration. The superstructure with perimeter pilasters throughout and an attic zone is modelled on St. Peter’s in Rome, as is the building’s basic design with domed tri-conch. The tower, expressing the motif of the Trinity, was originally designed with a spiral-shaped pinnacle.

976874d7-3e8f-5368-ba10-5054c2f2a238.name: Oil paintings
976874d7-3e8f-5368-ba10-5054c2f2a238.description: Three examples of the six oil paintings that make up the Cycle of the Life of the Virgin and the Childhood of Jesus.
976874d7-3e8f-5368-ba10-5054c2f2a238.artist: Attributed to Bento Coelho da Silveira's workshop, Lisbon (1648–1708)

9779dbd4-5cc7-5f2e-8017-625b454897d3.name: High altar
9779dbd4-5cc7-5f2e-8017-625b454897d3.description: The powerful, Early Baroque high altar, which was reworked in the 18th century, is one of the earliest two-leveled conceptions in Bavaria serving a pilgrimage cult. Statues of the bishopric patron, St. Ulrich, and the order’s patron, St. Augustine, stand between pillars. A fold-away altarpiece painting referring to the legend of the pilgrimage once stood at the centre of the altar, behind this would have been an upper altar that was reserved for a spiritual dignitary. The miraculous, legendarily supposed Thassilo-Crucifix which replaced the painting in reality dates from about 1230. The front of the crucifix shows an image of Christ crucified covered with horse skin. This originally would have been placed near to the pilgrims on the lower altar. In the 18th century, Johann Baptist Straub used the space vacated by the crucifix for a marvelous tabernacle with figures of the Holy Emperor Heinrich and his wife Kunigunde as well as allegories of Faith, Hope and Love. Sensitively rendered reliefs appear typologically on the sacrifice of the mass: the Harvest of Manna, the Last Supper and Supper at Emmaus.
9779dbd4-5cc7-5f2e-8017-625b454897d3.artist: Hans Krumpper (1570–1634); Benedikt Meggas; Bartholomäus Steinle (1580–1628/29); Johann Baptist Straub (1704–1784)

9907ee8c-c9bc-5075-a64d-986d4821b30a.name: Vault with stucco and ceiling paintings
9907ee8c-c9bc-5075-a64d-986d4821b30a.description: The ceiling frescos, framed by delicate strapwork stucco, were painted by Franz Laukas from Prutz. The five large panels depict scenes from the life of Mary, accompanied by eight smaller Mariological pictures and six scenes depicting the legend of the pilgrimage. Laukas’s painting style displays a clear folk art element – in particular the smaller panels with their charming naivety reminiscent of votive painting.
9907ee8c-c9bc-5075-a64d-986d4821b30a.artist: Franz Laukas (1690–1765); Anton Gigl (1700–1769), Augustin Gigl (dates unknown, active in the first half of the 18th century)

9a119226-14e5-5c76-9358-4559912ca023.name: Chapel of Our Lady of the Doctrine
9a119226-14e5-5c76-9358-4559912ca023.description: The main image of this chapel represents Our Lady of the Doctrine (St. Ann with the Virgin Mary in her arms). Although the chapel was built in the 17th century, the decoration is typical of the Portuguese Baroque “National style”, which developed during the late 17th and early 18th century. This side chapel is the only one where gilded woodwork covers the whole of the interior surface including the barrel-vaulted ceiling.
9a119226-14e5-5c76-9358-4559912ca023.dates: Work on the chapel began on 1 April 1634 and it was used by the Brotherhood of Our Lady of the Doctrine as their headquarters. The stonework was finally completed in 1690.
9a119226-14e5-5c76-9358-4559912ca023.location: Church Interior, Church of São Roque
9a119226-14e5-5c76-9358-4559912ca023.artist: The woodwork is by José Rodrigues Ramalho (1660–1721) according to a contract dated 1688 between him and the Brotherhood. The stonework was executed by master masons, Manuel Antunes and João Teixeira, whose exact dates are unknown.

9ae03881-78f0-5e63-bd66-5bb57bff8346.name: Monk’s Choir
9ae03881-78f0-5e63-bd66-5bb57bff8346.description: Because of its stuccoed  stellar vault the oratory of the monks is counted as one of the most beautiful early Baroque rooms in Old Bavaria. A round dance of angels in its centre presents the instruments of passion of Christ.
9ae03881-78f0-5e63-bd66-5bb57bff8346.location: First floor of the chancel building
9ae03881-78f0-5e63-bd66-5bb57bff8346.artist: Architecture: Marx Schinnagl (1612–81); Stucco: Kaspar Feichtmayr the Elder (1639–1704)

9cf9544c-47c2-5741-bf3e-5d928fd5cfa2.name: Chapel of Our Lady of Piety
9cf9544c-47c2-5741-bf3e-5d928fd5cfa2.description: The design for the retable is centred on a representation of Calvary. A 17th-century sculpture of the Pietà completes the tribune. The wood carving is exuberantly multi-coloured as a result of the variety of gold leaf that covers it.
9cf9544c-47c2-5741-bf3e-5d928fd5cfa2.dates: The construction and decoration was overseen by the Brotherhood of Our Lady of Piety. According to an inscription, work began in September 1686 and was completed by 1711. The retable dates from 1708. The gilding was added in 1716.
9cf9544c-47c2-5741-bf3e-5d928fd5cfa2.location: Church Interior, Church of São Roque
9cf9544c-47c2-5741-bf3e-5d928fd5cfa2.artist: The retable was made by the 18th-century master carver Bento da Fonseca de Azevedo

a0121cc0-20a3-5469-8da2-4993a1e95a3a.name: Main façade
a0121cc0-20a3-5469-8da2-4993a1e95a3a.description: The end side facing the Untermarkt is the magnificently decorated main façade of the house with a central bay window. Architecture paintings form the structure and frame for the images. At the bay window the central motifs are presented, in the middle below the window the Mary Help picture from Innsbruck carried by putti, above it God the Father and the Holy Ghost. On the side walls further putti are depicted playing with a wind wheel and bird cage, while the putti to the side of the bay window present the Tablets of the Law with the Ten Commandments, the Cross of Christ and a chalice. The gable zone features a peacock. The overall appearance is primarily a result of the virtuoso rocaille frames around the windows. Cornice and gable, both painted, form the upper termination.

ab9ca50b-155a-5181-83a8-a7d112c0581e.name: Figure of the Divine Emperor
ab9ca50b-155a-5181-83a8-a7d112c0581e.description: A harmonious sculpture representing Christ Crucified, of which the anchor and sceptre are of filigree silver.

acbcd2fe-73a5-5680-ae25-a6b4c595a3b1.name: *Sala Terrena*
acbcd2fe-73a5-5680-ae25-a6b4c595a3b1.description: The space is decorated with illusionary ornamental painting evoking an overgrown pergola. The adjoining lounge contains Japanese genre scenes and “Roman” baths with stucco ornamentation decorated with shells and stones.
acbcd2fe-73a5-5680-ae25-a6b4c595a3b1.artist: Giovanni Michele Fontana, Johann Wenzl Bergl?

acdb77c0-0663-595b-975d-8751bfd3847c.name: Old Festival Hall
acdb77c0-0663-595b-975d-8751bfd3847c.description: The early Baroque festival hall, adorned with two magnificently columned doorways, underwent a reworking in the high Baroque style by means of fully plastical stucco. The allegorical ceiling paintings, complexly mirroring life, deal with the seasons; the elements of fire, water, air and earth; the animal, plant and mineral worlds; the eternal circle of virtue and vice; the work of Christ interpreted as hunter, fisherman and gardener; as well as the resulting triumph of the rational believing soul.
acdb77c0-0663-595b-975d-8751bfd3847c.dates:
1672–75 establishment  
Around 1690 replenishment of ceiling stucco
acdb77c0-0663-595b-975d-8751bfd3847c.location: Second floor of the convent floor west wing
acdb77c0-0663-595b-975d-8751bfd3847c.artist: Architecture: Marx Schinnagl (1612–81); Stucco: Kaspar Feichtmayr the Elder (1639–1704), Nicolò Perti or Prospero Brenno; ceiling paintings: Stephan (1622–1700) and Michael Kessler (born 1649)

b3631ca4-4c40-5863-ad39-0d6734c902ed.name: Blackamoor
b3631ca4-4c40-5863-ad39-0d6734c902ed.description: The figure of an adoring Blackamoor complements the iconography of the altar in the side chapel of St. Francis Xaverius added in 1670. The allegories of America and Asia symbolise the outreach of the Jesuit order. The ceiling painting features scenes from the saint’s missionary activities and is a sequel to the painting in the vault of the main nave: Ignatius of Loyola Spreading the Flame of Christ’s Faith to the Four Continents.
b3631ca4-4c40-5863-ad39-0d6734c902ed.location: Jesuit Church of the Assumption of the Virgin Mary

b7aa2d97-f660-5f39-a7c3-53ec68eec878.name: Victory Hall
b7aa2d97-f660-5f39-a7c3-53ec68eec878.description: The Regency-style panelled hall shows in its paintings, reliefs, concave moulding and ceiling fresco scenes of war, which refer to the Elector’s military success in the Turkish Wars. Scenes of the unsuccessful War of the Spanish Succession were deliberately avoided.
b7aa2d97-f660-5f39-a7c3-53ec68eec878.location: New Palace, first floor of the central wing
b7aa2d97-f660-5f39-a7c3-53ec68eec878.artist: Johann Adam Pichler (c. 1690–1761); Charles Dubut (c. 1687–1742): Jacopo Amigoni (c. 1682–1752); Joachim Beich (1665–1748)

b7c0b98d-c15d-53e7-87ca-e9455c41bd5a.name: Choir and crossing
b7c0b98d-c15d-53e7-87ca-e9455c41bd5a.description: Located at the centre of the building is the crossing, above which rises an octagonal cupola. A special feature is formed by the transitional pendentives, which here are filled in as opposed to being concavely arched. The tambour, studded with large windows, has an eight-sided cloister vault above it. The choir, considerably lower than the cross-arms due to its apse, has been under reconstruction since 2004 as part of the work on the high altar (from 1757) which was destroyed in 1943. The original altarpiece has been replaced by a work from Antonio Balestra from the story of St. Jacob. The straight-sided choir is flanked by two choir lofts, supported by stucco angels.

b9abc8a0-1fc1-59ad-9b41-3194b57afd27.name: Throne Room
b9abc8a0-1fc1-59ad-9b41-3194b57afd27.description: The Throne Room, also known as the Great Room, is the largest of the palace's three state rooms. Construction began in 1768 when the marriage of Dom Pedro to the future Queen Maria I demanded a large area for official audiences. Designed by the architect, Jean-Baptiste Robillion, the new room was built in the Rococo style with carvings by the sculptor and wood carver, Silvestre de Faria Lobo. The paintings on the ceiling represent Faith, Sun, Hope, War, Justice and Charity and were executed under the direction of the painter, João de Freitas Leitão. Manuel da Costa, António Berardi and Manuel do Nascimento assisted him.
b9abc8a0-1fc1-59ad-9b41-3194b57afd27.artist: Jean Baptiste Robillion (active 1758–1782); carving: Silvestre de Faria Lobo; painters: João de Freitas Leitão, Manuel da Costa, António Berardi, Manuel do Nascimento, whose dates are unknown.

bbb068e0-786d-5185-ae89-0a937e547d94.name: Ceiling fresco of the Dining Room
bbb068e0-786d-5185-ae89-0a937e547d94.description: The enchanting fresco on the ceiling of the Dining Room shows Odysseus’ arrival at the nymph Calypso’s island guarded in heaven by gods. It was painted primarily during the reign of Max III Joseph.
bbb068e0-786d-5185-ae89-0a937e547d94.location: New Palace, ground floor of the central wing

bd83431f-3b68-50c1-b369-a3b63fc107e1.name: Staircase
bd83431f-3b68-50c1-b369-a3b63fc107e1.description: A two-shouldered staircase with stucco decoration is overlooked by a ceiling painting of *The Fall of the Titans*. A number of Italian artists who had settled in Vienna worked for Count Questenberk in the 1720s and 30s.

bf8d5dd6-621c-537a-a14f-13c5c7464cea.name: Gardens
bf8d5dd6-621c-537a-a14f-13c5c7464cea.description: Expansion of the garden was possible after resolution of the uneven land quotas and the relatively rough excavation. The garden's first designer was the Dutchman, Jan van der Kolke, who followed the plans of Robillion. The expansion followed a structure typical of the Portuguese “farm”, purchasing the surrounding land to create a formal garden, a recreational garden and a large area for cultivation, the *Quinta Real*.
bf8d5dd6-621c-537a-a14f-13c5c7464cea.artist: Jean Baptiste Robillion (active 1758–1782); Garden statues: John Cheere (1709-1787)

bfde98ff-c1bf-5790-801d-18b84b741f38.name: Ceiling frescos: *Care of the Arts* – *Theological Truth* – *Profane Truth*
bfde98ff-c1bf-5790-801d-18b84b741f38.description: The central ceiling image of the library hall displays Theological Truth through Divine Revelation. In the next fresco, Parnassus as the Mountain of the Muses with feminine allegories shows the close relationship between the arts, and likewise, the close relationship between the monastery and the modern sciences. On the other side Truth, in the sense of profane critical science, is taken as a theme illustrating the “unveiling of truth”, which at the same time underlines the quintessence of the entire programme. The depiction is based on the title page of Diderot's *Encyclopédie*, the famous encyclopedia of the Enlightenment, which was perceived at the time to bring together the entirety of knowledge from the sciences, the arts and the trades. Provost Fanciscus Töpsl leaves behind his intellectual legacy by using his coat-of-arms: he sees himself not only as the third founder and decisive reformer of his foundation, but likewise, as father of its enlightened mission to instruct and inform.
bfde98ff-c1bf-5790-801d-18b84b741f38.location: Vault of the Library Hall, Augustinian Canons’ Convent of the Holy Saviour

c27eb774-cc9f-55db-b3e3-343e34b005f2.name: Middle room balcony railings
c27eb774-cc9f-55db-b3e3-343e34b005f2.description: Each room has a different colour scheme and decorative emphasis with multicoloured bookshelves of different lacquered finishes in green, red and black decorated with *chinoiserie* motifs. Each of the rooms is two-storeys high, with a balcony and stairs incorporated into the furniture.
c27eb774-cc9f-55db-b3e3-343e34b005f2.location: Interior, Biblioteca Joanina da Universidade de Coimbra
c27eb774-cc9f-55db-b3e3-343e34b005f2.artist: Design and execution: Francesco Gualdini, João Rodrigues de Almeida; supervisor: Gaspar Ferreira; painting and gilding of woodwork: Manuel da Silva [dates unknown]

c2fa115e-3ff1-53bd-a4fb-c6aa6c675900.name: Examples of *Via Crucis* chapels: Chapel of the Flagellation and the Mercury Fountain; Chapel of the Crucifixion and the interior of the Chapel of the Falls
c2fa115e-3ff1-53bd-a4fb-c6aa6c675900.description: The Stairway of the Five Senses leads up to the Crucifixion Chapel. On the way up are other chapels one of which, the Chapel of the Flagellation, reinforces the Suffering of Christ or the *Via Crucis* as an element of purification.
c2fa115e-3ff1-53bd-a4fb-c6aa6c675900.location: The Stairway of the Five Senses, Bom Jesus de Braga (Bom Jesus do Monte)

c4949ddb-d9d5-551d-b5df-1849fe2e8307.name: Ceremonial Façade (main façade)
c4949ddb-d9d5-551d-b5df-1849fe2e8307.description: Perhaps one of the best palace façades of the Portuguese Baroque, it combines traditional Portuguese features with Classical precision. The triangular pediment, adorned at the tympanum with garlands, averts the solemnity of a façade which is the keynote of the garden views.
c4949ddb-d9d5-551d-b5df-1849fe2e8307.location: Exterior view from the Pênsil Garden
c4949ddb-d9d5-551d-b5df-1849fe2e8307.artist: Jean Baptiste Robillion (active 1758–1782), Mateus Vicente de Oliveira (1706–1786)

cb0bfb98-65d7-5e00-ac6e-f7448d4fefe4.name: Feudal Hall
cb0bfb98-65d7-5e00-ac6e-f7448d4fefe4.description: Following the fire of 1752, J. Stern decorated both library and chapel ceilings. The restoration of the Feudal Hall (Courtroom) took place in parallel; its decoration featuring key scenes from the history of the Olomouc bishopric and the apotheosis of the builder, Bishop Egkh. A virtuoso fresco with a striking colour scheme, it is considered one of the most impressive of its kind in Central Europe.
cb0bfb98-65d7-5e00-ac6e-f7448d4fefe4.artist: Franz Anton Maulbertsch (1724 Langenargen am Bodensee – 1796 Vienna), František Ondřej Hirnle (1726, Prague – 1774, Kroměříž)

cee30618-4395-58d9-9364-6ae0526dbf95.name: Church of St. Margaret
cee30618-4395-58d9-9364-6ae0526dbf95.description: The church, with an oval nave, presbytery and vestibule, is 20.2 m long, 14.8 m wide and 44 m high. Its fresco decoration is the apotheosis of St. Margaret. She is accompanied by two angels, crypto-portraits of the investor and his wife, Marie Antonie of Friedberg–Scheer. The nave contains six side altars. The two front altars feature reliquaries of two young martyrs, Saints Vincent and Reparata, presented by Pope Innocent XII to the count during his journey to Rome. The church joined the chateau and the area below it. The concept is not only of architectural importance but also manifests the connection between the sovereign and the people, considered an aspect of “beneficent reign”.
cee30618-4395-58d9-9364-6ae0526dbf95.artist: Johann Lucas von Hildebrandt (1668 Genoa – 1745 Vienna), František Antonín Findt, Karel František Tepper (1682–1738), Kaspar Ober

cfe4e76b-dae8-5b07-88b5-6d61d4cac871.name: Relic chapel
cfe4e76b-dae8-5b07-88b5-6d61d4cac871.description: What is commonly known as the *Achbergkapelle* (Relic Chapel), so-called due to a miraculous sculptured image of the Virgin Mary, contains a splendid stucco marble altar wall with integrated relic shrines and atmospheric Neapolitan-influenced oil paintings on the ceiling depicting the Life of Christ.
cfe4e76b-dae8-5b07-88b5-6d61d4cac871.location: Ground floor of the choir, to the right of the presbytery, Augustinian Canons’ Convent of the Holy Saviour

d0ab1550-cbd5-5935-b8c4-fe0633742da9.name: Neptune Fountain
d0ab1550-cbd5-5935-b8c4-fe0633742da9.description: The Neptune Fountain is perhaps one of the most remarkable pieces of 17th-century Baroque stonework in Portugal. Originating during the period of the Castelo Melhor, the fountain was commissioned in Rome shortly after 1675 , 1675 by Luis de Meneses, Count of Ericeira and Portuguese Ambassador in Rome, and made specifically for his Lisbon palace of Anunciada where it was installed in the gardens. After the earthquake of 1755, the fountain fell into the hands of other owners and ended up in several different locations. It was finally purchased by the state and placed in the gardens of Queluz in the first half of the 20th century. Today we know it was probably commissioned from Gian Lorenzo Bernini (the *“vernino*” as he is referred to in Portuguese documentation) who delegated work on it to Ercole Ferrata.

d1138bd2-9ece-57a8-a87f-358caf766c14.name: *Azulejos*
d1138bd2-9ece-57a8-a87f-358caf766c14.description: *Azulejos* illustrating the story of Joseph in Egypt captioned in Latin. At the bottom of each panel the Miracles of S. Gonçalo of Amarante are represented.
d1138bd2-9ece-57a8-a87f-358caf766c14.location: Four *Azulejos* panels (two per side) line the lower register of the church walls, interrupted by the pulpit and stairs.
d1138bd2-9ece-57a8-a87f-358caf766c14.artist: Attributed to Teotónio dos Santos [n.d.], Lisbon tile production

d3d037ed-e8e5-5ff3-85c2-555bbabfcf8d.name: New Festival Hall (Princely Hall; now the convent chapel of the Salesian monastery)
d3d037ed-e8e5-5ff3-85c2-555bbabfcf8d.description: The Festival Hall, ideally conceptualised for the reception of Bavarian electoral princes as sovereigns, is decorated in the courtly Régence style. The central ceiling painting illustrates the establishment of the abbey as if it occurred in the present day at the time. This reinforces the ambivalent relationship between monastic allegiance and welfare provided by the sovereign.
d3d037ed-e8e5-5ff3-85c2-555bbabfcf8d.location: First floor in the south wing of the arcade court
d3d037ed-e8e5-5ff3-85c2-555bbabfcf8d.artist: Stucco and frescoes: Johann Baptist (1680–1758) and Johann Joseph (1707–43) Zimmermann

d721d07e-af8d-5c90-a2d1-60b3a0ac2fd3.name: Altar of the Holy Kinship
d721d07e-af8d-5c90-a2d1-60b3a0ac2fd3.description: The Altar of the Holy Family (or more broadly the Holy Kinship), with its altarpiece, is a reference to the Bavarian dynasty and the future of Christian Bavaria. The theme of the Annunciation of the Virgin is carried through in the imagery of the altar; the painting, the figures of saints either side, and the predella panel at the bottom. The altar can be seen therefore to indicate the birth of the Crown Prince and reiterate the dedicational background of the church. At one time the altarpiece in the choir (now destroyed) also picked up on this votive purpose.

d8c1fd87-1ac6-5fe2-b25b-54927d0e8b27.name: Ecce Homo (“day’s work” or *giornata* of the presbytery fresco)
d8c1fd87-1ac6-5fe2-b25b-54927d0e8b27.description: The Ecce Homo group over the high altar with the statue of the Scourged Christ represents Jesus as the victor over earthly tribulations. The contours outline the “day's work” – *giornata –* showing individual phases of the painting for which fresh plaster had to be applied and into which the artist could paint for up to three days. The sections also show the division of labour between the artist of the illusionary architecture and the painter of the figures.
d8c1fd87-1ac6-5fe2-b25b-54927d0e8b27.location: Pilgrimage Church of the Scourged Saviour, Dyje
d8c1fd87-1ac6-5fe2-b25b-54927d0e8b27.artist: Franz Anton Maulbertsch (1724 Langenargen am Bodensee – 1796 Vienna) and associates

e6d1474a-473c-5669-a0d5-a4ba232d0192.name: Interior, facing east
e6d1474a-473c-5669-a0d5-a4ba232d0192.description: The actual sacred centre of the church is the Chapel of Mercy with the devotional picture of Mary, an oval structure at the central axis of the nave. The hall of the church is surmounted by a depressed barrel vault in which deep lunettes are cut. The walls are structured by simple pilasters. The heavily retracted choir of steeper proportions receives considerably more light than the nave and thus stages the high altar as the second focal point of the space, opposite the Chapel of Mercy.

e8770573-d328-5834-b1d9-a0c8ce5da0f6.name: Bom Jesus Church
e8770573-d328-5834-b1d9-a0c8ce5da0f6.description: At ground level there are two sculptural figures of the prophets, Jeremiah and Isaiah. Over the cornice, on the upper section, are the four evangelists.
e8770573-d328-5834-b1d9-a0c8ce5da0f6.location: Façade of the church in the Neo-Classical style, Bom Jesus de Braga (Bom Jesus do Monte)

ee0459a7-7135-59f3-8a2f-96ace2250f9f.name: Ceiling fresco
ee0459a7-7135-59f3-8a2f-96ace2250f9f.description: Already on the staircase, the profession, rank and claim to power of von Liebenhofen are demonstrated. The ceiling is decorated with an oval fresco by Guglielmi, framed within gold-plated stucco. Its theme is the benefices of trade for the arts and sciences.

f2e3163a-4308-51ca-8274-354207600f17.name: General view of the Sacristy
f2e3163a-4308-51ca-8274-354207600f17.description: The redesigned sacristy with marble floor and a marble table. The coat of arms of the Franciscans and of the Royal family are fashioned in *Azulejos,* above which are a series of paintings with religious themes. A Brazilian ebony chest of drawers with a Rococo gilded carved back furnishes one end.
f2e3163a-4308-51ca-8274-354207600f17.artist: Woodcarver: Félix Adauto da Cunha (1649–c.1703); painter André Gonçalves (1685–1762)

f2fd7abc-465f-5f55-a1af-5082af90fafa.name: Sacristy
f2fd7abc-465f-5f55-a1af-5082af90fafa.description: The sacristy holds a large chest of drawers form the 17th century. On its wooden back board is a set of 20 paintings from the Life of St. Francis Xavier.
f2fd7abc-465f-5f55-a1af-5082af90fafa.location: Church interior, Sacristy, Church of São Roque

fb2c16ce-05ab-5038-b941-2740a8a0e2cb.name: Detail of ceiling painting
fb2c16ce-05ab-5038-b941-2740a8a0e2cb.description: The *Trompe l'oeil* ceiling painting depicts three manifestations of Wisdom: an allegory of the library (*Bibliotheca*), of the university (*Universitas*) and of the encyclopaedia (*Encyclopaedia*).
fb2c16ce-05ab-5038-b941-2740a8a0e2cb.location: Interior, Biblioteca Joanina da Universidade de Coimbra
fb2c16ce-05ab-5038-b941-2740a8a0e2cb.artist: António Simões Ribeiro and Vicente Nunes [n.d.]

fb3fdb2d-573f-563d-9108-61663265d16a.name: Portrait of João V
fb3fdb2d-573f-563d-9108-61663265d16a.description: The portrait of the King João V emerges from a sort of a “*rideau de scène*” in carved wood, upheld by angels. The oil on canvas painting is by Domenico Duprà, royal painter in Lisbon before 1730.
fb3fdb2d-573f-563d-9108-61663265d16a.location: Interior, Biblioteca Joanina da Universidade de Coimbra

fc094f04-ed4e-5c5a-b47f-7bcc11b75d8f.name: The Chapel of Santo António  or Ante-Choir
fc094f04-ed4e-5c5a-b47f-7bcc11b75d8f.description: The beautiful floors of the Chapel of Santo António are of inlaid Brazilian wood. *Azulejo* panels – representing scenes from the lives of the hermit saints Anthony and Paul – adorn the walls on the lower register, while on the upper register are paintings depicting the Miracles of St Anthony of Lisbon. Behind a monumental door is the Madre de Deus crib, comprising a set of 42 sculpted polychrome terracotta figures.
fc094f04-ed4e-5c5a-b47f-7bcc11b75d8f.artist: André Gonçalves (1685–1762); terracotta figures in crib: António Ferreira [n.d.] and Dionísio Ferreira [n.d.]
